claims: The Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) of 1978 is a U.S. federal law.
FISA establishes procedures for physical and electronic surveillance of foreign intelligence on domestic soil.
FISA established the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court (FISC).
FISC oversees warrant requests primarily targeting foreign powers and agents.
Section 702 allows warrantless targeting of non-U.S. persons outside the U.S.
Section 702 often captures Americans' data.
FISA was enacted to prevent illegal warrantless surveillance of Americans.
FISA authorizes, limits, and regulates surveillance for foreign intelligence gathering.
FISC is a specialized court.
FISC reviews and approves applications for surveillance warrants and physical searches.
Under Section 702, FISC reviews targeting procedures.
Section 702 allows targeting of non-U.S. persons located outside the U.S. to gather foreign intelligence.
Section 702 often involves US electronic communication service providers.
Section 702 does not require an individual warrant for each target.
Section 702 relies on court-approved targeting and minimization procedures, as detailed on Intelligence.gov.
FISA has been amended in 2008.
As of April 2026, Congress is debating the reauthorization of Section 702.
Section 702 is set to expire on April 20.
Some lawmakers are proposing attaching the Save America Act.
The Save America Act would add a requirement of proof of citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.
The Save America Act would add a requirement of the presentation of an ID to cast a ballot
